samples: This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table covering -10 to 40 degrees Celsius in steps of 10, with a header row and right-aligned columns. It also provides a public, pure conversion function that you can reuse elsewhere, and it includes built-in examples checking the freezing point, the boiling point and -40. It needs only console output, with no files, network or other side effects, so it is safe to run. The range and step are fixed in the code, so a different table means editing the program.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion table, covering -10 to 40 degrees Celsius in steps of 10, with the two columns right-aligned under a header. It also exposes a reusable conversion function that turns a Celsius decimal into Fahrenheit, and that function carries built-in examples checking freezing, boiling and the -40 crossover point. It is a simple, pure-computation demo that needs only console output, so it's safe to run but too small to be useful beyond a template or a quick reference table.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table for -10 through 40 degrees in steps of 10, with a header and right-aligned columns. It also exposes a reusable, pure conversion function with built-in examples (freezing, boiling, and the -40 crossover). It only needs console output, so it's safe and simple to use, but the range and step are fixed in the code rather than configurable.

This program prints a small Celsius to Fahrenheit table, covering temperatures from -10 to 40 degrees in steps of 10, under a "Celsius  Fahrenheit" header with right-aligned columns. It also offers a reusable, public conversion function that turns one Celsius value into Fahrenheit, and its built-in examples check the freezing point, boiling point and -40. It only needs console output, with no files, network or other side effects, so it is safe to run and a good small example, but the range and step are fixed in the code rather than configurable.

This program prints a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion table covering -10 to 40 degrees in steps of 10, with a header line and right-aligned columns. It also provides a reusable, documented function that converts a single Celsius value to Fahrenheit, with built-in examples checking freezing, boiling and the -40 crossover. It's a small, self-contained demo that needs only console output, so it's safe to run, but the fixed range means you'd have to edit it to get a different table.
